guide.summary: Notion documents user OAuth for integrations installed in customer workspaces; each user authorizes and picks pages to share. The only grant needed is the Read content capability, a capability rather than an OAuth scope string, and the integration must not request update or insert.
guide.recommendation: Notion documents user OAuth for integrations installed in customer workspaces; each user authorizes and picks pages to share. The only grant needed is the Read content capability, a capability rather than an OAuth scope string, and the integration must not request update or insert.

findings.title: Per-user OAuth with page picker; token tied to the authorizing user
findings.detail: The user opens the authorization URL, sees the connection's capabilities, selects pages in the page picker, and is redirected with a temporary code. The app exchanges the code at the token endpoint for an access_token and refresh_token. Each workspace member must authorize individually.
findings.appliesWhen: Customers connect their own workspaces and share pages with the integration.

findings.title: Read content capability
findings.detail: Read content lets a connection read existing content and is the capability recommended for exporting data out of Notion. Retrieve a page and Retrieve block children require read content, and missing capabilities return 403. Do not request update or insert content.
findings.appliesWhen: Reading page titles and content; no create or modify.

evidence.quote: * **Read content**: This capability gives a connection access to read existing content in a Notion workspace. For example, a connection with only this capability is able to call Retrieve
* If your connection is reading data to export it out of Notion, your connection will only need **Read content** capabilities.
## Errors The connection needs read content capabilities. Missing capabilities return `403`. A missing page or missing access returns `404`.

findings.title: Only pages the user shares are accessible, including children
findings.detail: The page picker shows only pages the user has full access to. Sharing a parent page gives access to its child pages. Unshared pages return errors, such as 404 for missing access.
findings.appliesWhen: Reading titles and content of shared pages.

evidence.quote: > [!NOTE] > > The page picker only displays pages or databases to which a user has full access, because a user needs full access to a resource in order
Page picker interface Users can select which pages to give the connection access to, including both private and public pages available to them. Parent pages can be selected to quickly
> [!NOTE] > > **If a connection is added to a page, then the connection can access the page’s children**

steps.title: Create the public OAuth integration in the Developer portal
steps.detail: In the Notion Developer portal create a connection with installation scope Any workspace (customers connect their own workspaces; scope cannot change after creation). Enter the redirect URI and enable ONLY the Read content capability; do not enable Update content, Insert content or any admin capability. Copy the OAuth client ID, OAuth client secret and authorization URL from the Configuration tab and store them as secrets.
steps.doneWhen: Integration exists with redirect URI, Read content only, and client ID/secret/auth URL stored securely.

steps.title: Send a test user to the Notion consent URL and verify the callback
steps.detail: Build the URL https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize?owner=user&client_id=<CLIENT_ID>&redirect_uri=<URL_ENCODED_REDIRECT_URI>&response_type=code&state=<RANDOM_STATE>. A test customer user opens it, reviews the capabilities and picks representative test pages in the page picker, then clicks Allow access. Your callback must verify state matches and read the code query parameter; an error=access_denied parameter means the user cancelled. This step is performed by a human user and is not executed by this guide.
steps.doneWhen: Callback received with matching state and a temporary code parameter (not an error).

steps.title: Read a shared page and its title
steps.detail: Use a page ID the test user shared (visible via the page URL or provided by you). Expected: 200 with the page object. The title is the entry in $.properties whose type is title; the key is dynamic (often Name or title), so find the property with type title. Join all plain_text values of the title array. Boundary check: request a page the user did NOT share and expect 404; also inspect the integration capabilities in the portal to confirm only Read content is enabled (a read-only grant is enforced by capability, never test a write).
steps.doneWhen: 200 returned and the title text assembled from $.properties.*.title[].plain_text; unshared page returns 404.

evidence.quote: Retrieves a page object by ID. The response includes page property values. To read the page’s content, use Retrieve block children.
Response JSON paths for GET /v1/pages/{page_id}: $.properties.*.title[].plain_text (string)
## Errors The connection needs read content capabilities. Missing capabilities return `403`. A missing page or missing access returns `404`.

fields: PAGE_ID: id of a page the user shared in the page picker
ACCESS_TOKEN: access_token from the token exchange

steps.title: Read the complete title property (first page of property items)
steps.detail: A page response truncates inline mentions in title to 25, so read the full title with the property item endpoint using the property ID of the title property (from $.properties.*.id in the page response). Expected: list; concatenate every $.results[].title.plain_text across pages. Continue while has_more is true.
steps.doneWhen: First page returned with results; has_more and next_cursor recorded. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

steps.title: Read page content blocks (first page)
steps.detail: The page ID is also a block ID; list its children. Expected: results array of blocks. Text is in each block's rich_text, for example $.results[].paragraph.rich_text[].plain_text; child pages use $.results[].child_page.title. Join all plain_text segments. This returns direct children only; for results with has_children true, run the nested follow-up step. Boundary check: request children of an unshared block and expect 404/403 rather than content. Initial children listing; record $.has_more and $.next_cursor. End condition: has_more is false.
steps.doneWhen: 200 with results; has_more and next_cursor recorded; blocks with has_children noted. First page read; next_cursor captured when has_more is true.

preparation.title: Registration worksheet
preparation.text:
Create the public OAuth integration in the Developer portal
In the Notion Developer portal create a connection with installation scope Any workspace (customers connect their own workspaces; scope cannot change after creation). Enter the redirect URI and enable ONLY the Read content capability; do not enable Update content, Insert content or any admin capability. Copy the OAuth client ID, OAuth client secret and authorization URL from the Configuration tab and store them as secrets.
Fields: redirect_uri: your HTTPS callback registered in the portal, client_id: Configuration tab, client_secret: Configuration tab
